id_green_acres.blurb: Green Acres is a small cliff in the Black Cliffs area along the Boise River east of Boise, on the south side of the water. It holds 13 climbs, nearly all of them traditional crack lines plus a single bolted route. Grades start at 5.9 and climb into the low 5.11s, split fairly evenly between the 5.9s and 5.10s with a few harder ones. The wall faces north, so it stays cool and shaded, and it rewards climbers who carry a rack and like to jam. A large part of the face has come down in the past, so be watchful of loose debris on the slope below. Expect a hike up from the river before a single-track path leads to the base.

id_left_of_the_alcove.blurb: A short band of basalt at Dierkes Lake in the Snake River Canyon near Twin Falls, running along the cliff just left of the big overhanging Alcove. It holds 13 routes: mostly sport and trad, with a couple of top-rope lines. Grades run from about 5.6 to 5.13, but the bulk sit around 5.10, and climbers say they feel harder than they look. The cliff faces south and takes sun all day, which suits cooler months. It is much lower than the Alcove itself, and its easier lines make it a popular place to set up top ropes. From the lake parking area a clear trail leads to the base of the band.

id_parking_lot_rock_west.blurb: The west-facing side of Parking Lot Rock in City of Rocks, southern Idaho, only a minute or so on foot from the road end. It has 13 routes, mostly trad with a few bolted lines and a top-rope, running from about 5.6 to 5.10 with plenty of moderates in the 5.8 range and a solid group of 5.10s. The granite lines are tall, so plan on a 70 m rope or double ropes to get back down. The wall is shaded in the morning and sunny in the afternoon. It is a busy crag, so expect to wait your turn on the popular lines.
id_parking_lot_rock_west.parking_note: From the main City of Rocks road, turn right at the King on the Throne formation and follow the short spur road to the lot at the foot of Parking Lot Rock.

id_window_rock_east.blurb: The back side of Window Rock in City of Rocks, southern Idaho, a low-angle granite slab that is a favourite with beginners, families and large groups. Most of its 13 routes are cracks protected by trad gear, with a few bolted or mixed lines and one top-rope; grades run from 5.6 up to the low 5.11s, with most between 5.7 and 5.9. Good rests and decent protection make it a gentle place for novices and a handy warm-up. The slab gets morning sun and afternoon shade. Many climbs end without fixed anchors, so be ready to build your own.
id_window_rock_east.parking_note: Use the same lot that serves Parking Lot Rock, then continue on foot from there.
id_window_rock_east.approach: Walk the trail toward Parking Lot Rock and branch north past it to reach Window Rock, then continue around to the back side where the slab sits.
